title: The Counter That Remembers
explanation:
A `static` local is initialised once, the first time control reaches it, and then lives until the program ends, so each call to `counter()` sees the previous value: 1, 2, 3. A plain local `n` is created fresh on every call, so `fresh()` always returns 1.

Why `123` and not `321`: since C++17, the operands of a `<<` chain are evaluated left to right. Before C++17 the order of the calls was unspecified, and this line could legally print `321`.
try_this: Make `counter` return `n++` instead of `++n`. What changes?
